title: Elastic backoff safeguard and KV-consistency patch for 5xx escalations
creator: Maya Chen
description: Customer escalations during the last tenant surge revealed a cascade: transient backend slowdowns triggered client retries that amplified proxy fanout and caused intermittent 5xx responses plus KV cache inconsistencies under heavy eviction. This ticket implements a short-term safety patch (elastic backoff + per-tenant request shaping) and a correctness fix to reduce KV cache races during eviction and compaction. Goal: stop customer-visible 5xx waves within the hour after rollout and provide a durable plan to prevent recurrence in future tenant bursts.
reproduction_steps: 1) Replay tenant burst using staging load-generator with 5x baseline RPS and variable inter-arrival jitter
2) Enable aggressive client retry policy (3 retries, immediate backoff) to simulate amplification
3) Force kvcache compaction while load is peaking (simulate eviction pressure)
4) Observe proxy fanout, upstream request queue lengths, and 5xx rate at the router and model server layers
5) Check kvcache metrics for stale entries, compaction races, and missing prefix hits
implementation_notes: A. Elastic backoff: introduce per-tenant token bucket that gates retry fanout and enforces exponential backoff caps for retries originating from internal SDKs and Gateway. SDK change will honor Retry-After headers from gateway.

B. Graceful degrade: When tenant token bucket is exhausted, immediately route new requests to a lightweight fast-path 'limited' model variant (cpu-quantized) with explicit response header X-Redwood-Degraded: true so clients can surface fallback UI.

C. KV consistency patch: serialize compaction with a short-lived optimistic lock and publish a compaction epoch header to avoid serving requests against partially compacted state. Add a post-compaction validation pass on staging that replays a subset of inflight prefixes.
D. Circuit integration: adjust circuit-breaker thresholds to prefer 429 (rate-limited) over 5xx where upstream latency is the root cause, so retries collapse gracefully.
E. Backwards compatibility: gateway will default to new token-bucket behavior; old SDKs will be treated as unthrottled for one cycle and then blocked with deprecation header to force upgrade path.
G. Tests: unit tests for compaction lock, integration test harness for tenant burst, chaos test toggling compaction epoch and network delays
acceptance_criteria: Deployed gateway patch reduces 5xx rate from burst runs by >=90% in staging for 10x baseline traffic within the same latency SLO window
KV compaction no longer produces stale-key access in 1000-run replay tests; zero observed compaction-induced 5xx in test harness
SDK clients receive clear X-Redwood-Degraded header and Retry-After behavior in degraded path
Runbook updated and on-call rotations briefed; playbook contains commands to toggle token-bucket thresholds per-tenant
Customer escalations referenced in parent issue receive a triage update and mitigation summary
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Canary deploy to 5% of gateway instances and a non-critical tenant cohort. Monitor 5xx, latency p90/p99, and kvcache compaction metrics for 30 minutes
Phase 1: If stable, increase to 25% and enable compaction-epoch validation in staging mirror; validate no increase in latency beyond +5%
Phase 2: Full cluster rollout with rolling restarts, enabling graceful degrade fast-path by default
Kill-switch: Rollback script that disables elastic backoff and restores previous kvcache behavior (automated via deployment pipeline)
monitoring: Alerts: paging if 5xx-rate > 1% for more than 5 minutes on >10 tenants OR token-bucket hit-rate > 80% for >2 minutes
SLO checks: ensure p95 generation latency within pre-rollout baseline +/- 10%
Audit logs: record compaction-epoch and per-request degradation headers for post-incident forensics
